title: Write Borrows (&mut)
story: &mut is exclusive — like giving someone a pen to write in your book. Nobody else can read or write while they have it.
why: &mut enforces exclusive access at compile time, eliminating data races and accidental mutation conflicts without any runtime locks.
analogy: &mut is like having the only key to a room and a whiteboard marker. You can go in, change things, and nobody else can enter until you come out.
try_it: Try creating a & and a &mut to the same Vec at the same time. See the compiler error about conflicting borrows.
tips: &mut means exclusive write access — no other references can exist
Use var (mutable binding) when you plan to create &mut references
The borrow ends when the &mut is last used, not at the end of scope (non-lexical lifetimes)
&mut prevents data races at compile time — no runtime locks needed
common_mistakes: Trying to create &mut from a let (immutable) binding — use var instead
Forgetting that &mut excludes even read borrows while it exists
Creating &mut then trying to use the original variable directly while the borrow is live
